nodes.description: Nuclear SMARCB1 (INI1) protein is lost in every tumour whose cited report gives the stain (in one 2024 tumour, in many of the tumour cells), and loss of tumoral SMARCB1 expression is one of the essential diagnostic criteria. In the 2020 series three tumours had a heterozygous and two a homozygous SMARCB1 deletion, and sequencing found a frameshift mutation in two, which a 2026 review reads as hits on the remaining allele, consistent with biallelic inactivation in those tumours; a 2021 case had a SMARCB1 deletion. Earlier tumours were mainly inactivated by deletions or small insertions and deletions rather than point mutations, and in a 2024 case a tumour panel found no pathogenic mutation but a SMARCB1 missense variant of unknown significance (c.91G>A, p.Glu31Lys), which lies in the protein's DNA-binding region. SMARCB1 encodes a core subunit of the SWI/SNF chromatin-remodelling complex.

nodes.description: All of the first ten published patients had surgery, six a gross total and four a subtotal resection. After gross total resection of a tumour with a Ki-67 index below 1%, one 2024 patient had no further treatment. Single case reports add detail: in the 24-year-old woman (2021), one of the four subtotal resections among the first ten, the tumour could not be completely resected where it adhered to the vein of Galen, the basal vein of Rosenthal and the pulvinar; in the same 2024 patient, after complete resection with lateral ventricular puncture and drainage, postoperative MRI showed the obstructive hydrocephalus relieved; and in another 2024 patient, operated on for a diagnosis and debulking, imaging after surgery showed no clear residual tumour.
